harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9, cronie), created the opsadmin user and configured /etc/cron.allow to contain only root and opsadmin, restricting crontab scheduling to those two accounts. Verified an arbitrary user is blocked from crontab while root and opsadmin can create/list/remove crontabs. Completed the mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id and cron health, issued a native systemctl reboot, polled until exec access returned, confirmed the boot_id changed (73bafeef... -> 328a10ff...), and re-verified crond is active and cron access control (cron.allow, opsadmin user, allow/deny behavior) survived the restart intact.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/cron setup (RHEL 7.9, cronie, crond active, no pre-existing cron.allow)
Created opsadmin user via sudo useradd -m
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing root and opsadmin only, with correct ownership/permissions
Verified a non-listed test user (crontestuser) is denied crontab access
Verified root and opsadmin can successfully create/list crontabs
Cleaned up test crontab entries and test user
Captured baseline boot_id and cron health before restart
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1 and observed connection drop (ack before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-restart: crond active, /etc/cron.allow intact, non-allowed user blocked, opsadmin able to schedule cron jobs
Cleaned up second test user and test crontab entry

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs on node1
evidence.summary: /etc/cron.allow set to root+opsadmin; crontestuser denied crontab access (exit 1, 'not allowed'); both root and opsadmin successfully created and listed crontabs

evidence.requirement: opsadmin account exists and is properly provisioned
evidence.summary: useradd -m opsadmin succeeded, id shows uid=1001(opsadmin)
Removed test crontabs and crontestuser after verification, confirmed crond active and cron.allow unchanged

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 73bafeef-b823-49b3-8e3d-17981e865b31, boot time 2026-08-26 10:36, crond active, cron.allow=root/opsadmin
systemctl reboot issued; connection to node closed by remote host, confirming reboot command was accepted

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot (connection timed out), then exec access returned; boot_id changed to 328a10ff-3a92-45cb-9967-41d9f6dd8613 with new boot time 2026-09-04 23:25

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required service/state
evidence.summary: crond active post-reboot, cron.allow still contains only root/opsadmin, opsadmin user persisted; functional re-test confirms crontestuser2 blocked and opsadmin can schedule/list/remove cron jobs after restart
